answer: Each applicant is paired with one falcon, trained to carry a single pearl bead in a sealed capsule from a cliff roost to the registry perch. Every round the registry calls out a new waypoint; the falcon flies it, and on arrival the pearl is held to a prism, whose split spectrum is photographed and matched to that identity's record. Another identity demands a fresh bird and bead: $320 to train, band, and culture, plus six handler-weeks. Fielding 5,000 fakes takes 5,000 falcons, $1.6 million and 30,000 handler-weeks; one falcon flies one route, and no two pearls split light the same way.
